Extractor functions to access components of a permutation design

Source: R/getFoo-methods.R
get-methods.Rd

These functions provide abstracted access to components of permutation designs such as those returned by how(). Using them instead of directly indexing the underlying list allows that representation to evolve without breaking user code.

Usage

getAllperms(object, ...)

getBlocks(object, ...)

getComplete(object, ...)

getConstant(object, ...)

getCol(object, ...)

getDim(object, ...)

getMake(object, ...)

getMaxperm(object, ...)

getMinperm(object, ...)

getSymmetric(object, ...)

getObserved(object, ...)

getPlots(object, ...)

getRow(object, ...)

getWithin(object, ...)

getControl(object, ...)

getHow(object, ...)

Arguments

object

An R object on which to dispatch.

...

Arguments passed to other methods.

which

Character; the level of restriction for which information is required.

drop

Logical; should unused factor levels be dropped?

Value

The contents of the corresponding component of object.

Details

getHow() is an alias for getControl(); specific getControl() methods are useful when debugging.

See also

check() checks a permutation design described by how().

Author

Gavin Simpson

Examples

hh <- how()
getWithin(hh)
#> $type
#> [1] "free"
#> 
#> $constant
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $mirror
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $symmetric
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $ncol
#> NULL
#> 
#> $nrow
#> NULL
#> 
#> $call
#> Within()
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "Within"
getNperm(hh)
#> [1] 199
